input.prompt:
You are a Frama-C WP / ACSL annotation specialist. Your job: generate ACSL annotations for a single C file so that Frama-C WP proves its `//@ assert(...)` assertion, WITHOUT changing any original C tokens or assertions, and WITHOUT using admit/assume/axiom.

## Input source file (read this)
"[TASK]/workspace/output/layer0/main/main.c"

It contains a single function `main`:
- `int N = 100000;` global
- VLA arrays `int a[N]; int b[N];`
- Loop 1: for i in 0..N-1: `a[i] = i;`
- Loop 2: for i in 0..N-1: `b[N-i-1] = i;`
- Loop 3: for i in 0..N-1: `sum = sum + (a[i]-b[N-i-1]);`
- `//@assert(sum == 0);`

The assert is TRUE: b[N-i-1] = i means b[j] = N-1-j, and in loop 3 the term a[i]-b[N-i-1] = i - i = 0, so sum stays 0.

An inline reference (same function body, for understanding) is at:
"[TASK]/workspace/output/layer0/main/main.inline.c"

## Your task
Write an annotated version of the file to:
"[TASK]/workspace/output/layer0/main/main.acsl.c"

You only ADD ACSL comments (/*@ ... */ before loops, optional function contract before main); you must NOT modify, delete, or reorder any original C tokens or the `//@assert(sum == 0);` line.

### Required annotations
Give EVERY loop a block before the `for` with: `loop invariant`, `loop assigns`, `loop variant`. Notes:
- Loop 1 invariant: `0 <= i <= N;` and `\forall integer j; 0 <= j < i ==> a[j] == j;` assigns `i, a[0 .. N-1]`; variant `N - i`.
- Loop 2 invariant: `0 <= i <= N;` and `\forall integer j; 0 <= j < i ==> b[N-1-j] == j;` assigns `i, b[0 .. N-1]`; variant `N - i`.
- Loop 3: it reads arrays written by previous loops, so you MUST carry the full completed-array facts (range 0..N): `\forall integer j; 0 <= j < N ==> a[j] == j;` and `\forall integer j; 0 <= j < N ==> b[N-1-j] == j;`, plus `0 <= i <= N;` and `sum == 0;`. assigns `i, sum;`; variant `N - i`.

You may optionally add a function contract for main like `/*@ assigns \nothing; ensures \result == 0; */` — it is optional.

Use only standard ACSL. Do NOT use admit/assume/axiom anywhere. Do NOT add `\valid`/`\separated` admits.

## Verify it
Use this exact prefix for all spectool calls:
"/Users/dijkstra/ACSL-Agent 2/acsl模块化验证/.venv/bin/python" -m engine.harness_spectool

Run verify on your produced file:
"/Users/dijkstra/ACSL-Agent 2/acsl模块化验证/.venv/bin/python" -m engine.harness_spectool verify --file "[TASK]/workspace/output/layer0/main/main.acsl.c" --timeout 15 --save-stdout "[TASK]/workspace/output/layer0/main/main.wp.txt"

If result is not "Pass" (proved == total), inspect the .wp.txt failures and improve the loop invariants, then re-run verify. You may iterate up to 5 rounds. If you hit a ValueError/Invalid about `\result` being unusable in assigns for main, remove the function contract and keep only loop annotations. Target: all goals proved with result "Pass".

When done, report back in your final message:
- the final `proved`/`total` numbers and the `result` string from verify,
- confirm the original C tokens and the `//@assert(sum == 0);` line are byte-identical to the source,
- confirm zero admit/assume/axiom.

Do not modify any files other than producing output/layer0/main/main.acsl.c and main.wp.txt. Report the full final content of main.acsl.c.
